notes: The Hollow Sentinels of Mooring's Watch (bible 3.5, 6.1 quest 3 The Watch Still Stands; mw-e39.11), speaking as one voice: the armour stands in the tower hall still keep Sergeant Mooring's order, hold the tower. They are courteous and unmovable. The quest's six ways are the options: the watchword (any class, once the keeper's last leaf is read: evidence.keepers-last-leaf), the knight's formal relief, the archer's shot at the bell cord, the sorcerer dispelling the binding, the thief's unseen walk (they stay and keep their post) and smashing them (anyone, slow). Each sets sentinels.method; every way but the thief's also sets sentinels.relieved. The Sentinels are not placed yet (encounters are mw-e25.7), the creature stands in the debug conversation room; the bell cord shot, the dispel and the sneak are narrated here and become real with the placed Sentinels, spell.dispel and stealth.

nodes.speaker: sentinel
nodes.text: HALT. This tower is held. By order of Sergeant Aldric Mooring, no one passes the hall without the word.

nodes.speaker: sentinel
nodes.text: The word.

nodes.speaker: sentinel
nodes.text: The word, traveller. The tower is held.

options.text: Who is it you're holding the tower for?
How long ago was the order given?
I am a knight. By the old words of the watch, I relieve you.
(Loose an arrow at the bell cord hanging through the roof.)
(Unpick the order that binds you, thread by thread.)
(Wait for the change of the quarter-hour and slip past unseen.)
Then I'll take the tower from you.

nodes.speaker: sentinel
nodes.text: Then you do not pass. The keeper wrote everything down, traveller. His desk is in the quarters above, and he was never one to leave a thing unsaid.

nodes.speaker: sentinel
nodes.text: For the garrison. They marched out at dawn, under orders, and left the Sergeant, and the Sergeant left us the order. Someone will come back for us. Someone always comes back for the post.

nodes.speaker: sentinel
nodes.text: It is a long watch. We are not complaining. Sergeant Mooring wrote our names on the stands so we would be remembered. I am Ellis. I think. The paint has gone.

nodes.speaker: sentinel
nodes.text: Forty winters, by the count the tower keeps. The singing from the east began the second winter. We do not listen to it. We hold the tower.

nodes.speaker: sentinel
nodes.text: ...The word is right. The word is the Sergeant's own.

nodes.speaker: sentinel
nodes.text: Then you are a friend of the watch, and the watch is a very long one. Are you the relief?

options.text: The relief has come. Stand down. Go home.
Not yet. I only wanted to pass.

nodes.speaker: sentinel
nodes.text: Then pass, friend of the watch, and keep your voice down on the stairs. The men are tired.

nodes.speaker: sentinel
nodes.text: ...Those are the old words. They are the Sergeant's words, the ones he said we would hear when an officer came. Name your rank, knight.

nodes.speaker: sentinel
nodes.text: Then you have the right. We are relieved. Stand easy, all. Stand easy.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The arrow takes the frayed cord a hand below the roof beam. Far above, in a bell nobody has rung for forty years, something stirs and speaks one flat note.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: It is not the Vesper Bell. It is a soldier's bell, and every armour stand in the hall has turned its head toward it.

nodes.speaker: sentinel
nodes.text: That is the bell. The bell that ends the watch. Who rang it? ...It does not matter. It is rung. We are relieved.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The order is not a spell, exactly. It is a sentence that was said so firmly it grew a shape. You find the end of it, and pull, and the whole long line comes loose with a noise like a held breath being let go.

nodes.speaker: sentinel
nodes.text: Hold the... Hold the... what was it we were holding? The tower. Yes. The tower. For... For whom? Oh. Oh, we are tired.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The stands do not look away. They look at the door, and the stair, and the place a stranger would stand. You are not standing in any of those places.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: By the time the quarter-hour changes you have taken what is worth taking from the keeper's room, and the Sentinels have noticed nothing but a draught.

nodes.speaker: sentinel
nodes.text: The tower is held. By order of Sergeant Aldric Mooring. There has been a draught. There is always a draught.

nodes.speaker: sentinel
nodes.text: Then the order is plain. None passes who does not know the word. The watch will hold.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: It takes a long time. The Sentinels are slow and honourable and do not run, and they are very hard to knock down. When each one falls it says, quite quietly, that it is sorry about the post.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: At the last you stand in a hall of broken armour, and nothing is left to hold the tower but you.

nodes.speaker: sentinel
nodes.text: The post is relieved. Every stand, every man. We stood this watch for the Sergeant, and the Sergeant stood it for the garrison, and none of them came back.

nodes.speaker: sentinel
nodes.text: Thank you. Take the tower. Take the keys, traveller; they hang above the keeper's desk where the Sergeant left them. Tell the bell, if you pass it, that the watch is ended.

nodes.speaker: sentinel
nodes.text: ...Stand easy. The post is relieved. We are only armour, now, resting.

nodes.speaker: sentinel
nodes.text: The tower is held. We will be here.
